power.answer: Aer Lingus treats power banks as spare batteries: carry-on only, individually protected, not used or charged during the flight, with a maximum of 2 spare batteries per person unless the operator approves more.

sections.h: 🔋 What Aer Lingus says about power banks
sections.p: From the Aer Lingus Guide To Dangerous Goods (January 2026, revision 5 dated 14 April 2026), read on 22 November 2026.

head: Question
Aer Lingus rule
rows: Articles whose main purpose is a power source, such as power banks, are treated as spare batteries
Spare or loose lithium batteries in carry-on baggage only; the table marks checked baggage as not permitted
Watt-hour rating must not exceed 100 Wh
Lithium content must not exceed 2 g
Each person is limited to a maximum of 2 spare batteries; the operator may approve more
Each battery individually protected to prevent short circuit
Power banks must not be used or charged during the flight
Removable batteries must be taken out before the bag is checked and carried in the cabin

list: Not on the page: the guide's table gives no separate rule for batteries above 100 Wh; they are not permitted without operator approval.

faq: How many power banks can I take on Aer Lingus?
A maximum of 2 spare batteries per person, including power banks, unless the operator approves more.
Can I use my power bank on an Aer Lingus flight?
No. Power banks must not be used or charged during the flight.
Can I put a power bank in my checked suitcase on Aer Lingus?
No. Spare batteries and power banks must be carried in carry-on baggage only.
sources: Aer Lingus — Guide To Dangerous Goods (January 2026)
